reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: Caused by gain-of-function variants in TRPV4, a calcium-permeable cation channel; most cases are autosomal dominant, frequently arising de novo
The name reflects a 'changing' body proportion: relatively long trunk with short limbs at birth that evolves into a short trunk as progressive kyphoscoliosis develops
A small coccygeal skin-covered 'tail' overlying an elongated coccyx is a characteristic and highly suggestive external feature
Radiographs show severe platyspondyly with dumbbell-shaped shortened long bones due to marked metaphyseal flaring
Progressive kyphoscoliosis and cervical spine instability (odontoid hypoplasia, atlantoaxial subluxation) are the dominant clinical problems
Presents with a large joints that appear prominent, contractures, and restricted movement; joint hypermobility may coexist
The TRPV4 channelopathy spectrum overlaps other skeletal dysplasias (spondylometaphyseal dysplasia Kozlowski type) and neuropathies, so phenotype varies widely
reference.pathophysiology: Metatropic dysplasia results from gain-of-function variants in TRPV4, which encodes a widely expressed calcium-permeable transient receptor potential channel important in chondrocyte and osteoblast signalling. Abnormal channel gating disturbs endochondral ossification, producing severe platyspondyly and dumbbell-shaped long bones with exuberant metaphyseal flaring. The progressive nature reflects worsening vertebral collapse and kyphoscoliosis over time, which transforms an initially long trunk into a short trunk. Cervical instability arises from odontoid hypoplasia and ligamentous laxity, posing a risk of cord compression.
additionalInvestigations: Full skeletal survey to document platyspondyly, dumbbell long bones and metaphyseal flaring
TRPV4 molecular genetic testing (targeted or via a skeletal dysplasia panel)
Flexion-extension cervical spine imaging to assess atlantoaxial instability
Whole-spine imaging and monitoring for progressive kyphoscoliosis
Respiratory and sleep assessment where thoracic or cervical involvement threatens ventilation
redFlags: Cervical myelopathy or atlantoaxial instability threatening the spinal cord
Rapidly progressive kyphoscoliosis with thoracic insufficiency and respiratory compromise
New neurological deficit in limbs suggesting cord compression
Neonatal respiratory distress in severe early-presenting forms
reference.prognosis: Outcome depends on severity: milder cases have near-normal survival with orthopaedic morbidity, whereas severe forms cause significant respiratory and neurological compromise from thoracic restriction and cervical instability. Lifelong spinal surveillance is required.
pitfalls: Overlooking cervical instability before sedation, anaesthesia or manipulation, risking cord injury
Attributing the changing body proportions to a different evolving dysplasia and missing the diagnosis
Failing to recognise the coccygeal appendage as a diagnostic clue
Underestimating the pace of scoliosis progression and delaying orthopaedic referral
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
Bone Dysplasias: An Atlas of Genetic Disorders of Skeletal Development (Spranger)
management: Manage supportively as no drug corrects the TRPV4 channel defect, focusing on spinal, orthopaedic, and respiratory complications
Undertake cervical spine surveillance with flexion-extension imaging and proceed to surgical stabilisation or decompression for atlantoaxial instability or cord compression
Manage progressive kyphoscoliosis with bracing and spinal fusion surgery
Provide respiratory support for thoracic restriction, including ventilatory assistance and sleep assessment
Offer physiotherapy for joint contractures and mobility aids, with anaesthetic precautions to protect the unstable cervical cord
Coordinate care through a multidisciplinary team of clinical genetics, spinal and orthopaedic surgery, and respiratory medicine
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal dominant inheritance of TRPV4 variants, noting that many cases arise de novo
